Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-09
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Carlos Rivera, Leah O'Hara (Redwood) -- Anita Patel, Rafael Gomez, Sophie Lee, Tom Berg, Dina Farooq (LuminHealth)
Shared artifacts: Redwood MSA redline draft (link), SLA matrix spreadsheet (link), SOC2 summary (link), egress-cost-test-plan.xlsx (link)

[00:00:05] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um, we know there's a lot to cover — sla exceptions and the data transfer questions you flagged. quick roll call?
[00:00:15] Anita Patel: Anita here.
[00:00:18] Rafael Gomez: Rafael, CISO.
[00:00:20] Sophie Lee: Sophie, legal.
[00:00:22] Tom Berg: Tom, platform.
[00:00:24] Dina Farooq: Dina, data ops.
[00:00:27] Maya Chen: awesome. quick agenda: 1) MSA/DPA redline hotspots 2) SLA exceptions and how they impact acceptance criteria and pricing 3) cross-border egress and region routing, 4) next steps. Carlos will kick off with the SLA matrix.

[00:01:05] Carlos Rivera: thanks, maya. so we built an SLA matrix that maps latency, availability, and support response tiers to pricing bands. um, two things came up from your doc — first, the request for a 24x7 guaranteed p1 response within 30 minutes, and second, the indemnity/liability cap language you redlined to 2x fees rather than the standard 1x. just to align — our platform offers enterprise SLA tiers but certain operational guarantees for private onprem or VPC can differ.

[00:01:45] Sophie Lee: right, legal sees the 30 minute P1 as fairly strict. we typically require something like that only for customer-facing outages. for background processing pipelines we accept 2 hours. how does Redwood differentiate experience between hosted and dedicated?

[00:02:10] Leah O'Hara: good q. in hosted we provide multi-region routing and automated fallback; dedicated gives predictable throughput because you reserve capacity. p1 for hosted — we can commit 60 minutes for enterprise tier, 30 for dedicated with premium on-call add-on. there's also an automatic fallback to a smaller, lower-cost model variant which we can enable during capacity stress.

[00:02:42] Rafael Gomez: that fallback is a big signal for us — it impacts model fidelity and therefore compliance for certain clinical flows. we need the ability to opt-out of model fallback per-route — so if a route is patient-facing the system shouldn't degrade responses silently. is that possible?

[00:03:02] Carlos Rivera: yes, absolutely. we have per-route policies; you can pin a route to a model and disable fallback. that'll affect cost/latency and we can show the delta.

[00:03:18] Dina Farooq: second related thing — cross-border data transfer. Our legal requires PHI to never leave EU regions. how do we guarantee that? do you do region-locking and a strict VPC-only path? what about cache placement?

[00:03:36] Leah O'Hara: region-locking is supported on Private and Dedicated. for hosted we have region-aware routing and customer scoping of data residency; but note: prefix KV cache can be geo-replicated for performance unless explicitly disabled. we can configure caches to be region-local for your tenant. we'll document the cache behavior — it's a common gotcha.

[00:03:56] Tom Berg: okay cache geo-replication is actually a showstopper unless we can disable. can you confirm that's configurable per-tenant?

[00:04:06] Carlos Rivera: yes, per-tenant fine-grained config. we'll add that to the POC plan.

[00:04:20] Sophie Lee: on the MSA/DPA front — indemnity and liability caps. our procurement team wants a cap at 3x annual fees for gross negligence carve-out, and exceptions for data breach. Redwood's standard is indemnity limited to direct damages and a 1x fee cap. any wiggle room?

[00:04:42] Maya Chen: historically we try to keep liability caps to a multiple of fees — enterprise customers at committed volumes can get 2x or 3x with a contractual premium. for breaches we do carve-outs aligned to SOC2 obligations, and we have cyber-insurance that covers certain exposures. we can route this to legal for a commercial exception review; pricing will be impacted.

[00:05:00] Sophie Lee: can you share the cyber policy summary and insurer limits?

[00:05:05] Maya Chen: yes, we'll share the summary with redline MSA.

[00:05:12] [00:05:12] Rafael Gomez: encryption — KMS integration. we want BYOK and HSM-backed keys. how does Redwood integrate with customer KMS? is there support for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and on-prem HSM?

[00:05:30] Leah O'Hara: we have native integrations for AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault. BYOK flows are supported; HSM integrations require our private deployment and an HSM gateway — that's part of the Private plan. encryption at rest and in transit is standard across deployments. for hosted BYOK we rotate keys with your KMS, we don't extract plaintext keys.

[00:05:54] Tom Berg: if we do BYOK in hosted, what's the impact on latency for token decryption during inference?

[00:06:02] Carlos Rivera: negligible for normal flows because the KMS calls are for ephemeral prefix keys; the hot path uses a session key cached for short windows. we'll include microbenchmarks in the test tenant.

[00:06:18] Anita Patel: procurement is also asking about SSO/SAML and RBAC — we need SCIM provisioning for users, and audit logs shipped to their SIEM for 365 days. is that supported?

[00:06:31] Leah O'Hara: SCIM yes, SAML yes. audit logs can be exported to customer-owned S3 or syslog endpoint, there is a retention SLA — hosted default is 90 days, enterprise add-on 365 days. for private deployments we can match your retention. note there are egress/storage costs for long retention which we'll enumerate.

[00:06:55] Dina Farooq: good to know. where do billing/egress charges show up? our finance wants an egress forecast because the vendor wants a unit egress fee that could blow up our cost model.

[00:07:10] Carlos Rivera: right — egress costs: for hosted, network egress by region is charged per-GB and is separate from token pricing. for Dedicated/Private, if it's in your VPC we can offer blended pricing. we've prepared an egress-cost-test-plan — we'll run it against your sample traffic.

[00:07:30] Tom Berg: during the POC we want to test peak concurrency and small-latency tail p99. can Redwood run a burst test and show p50/p95/p99 for our 1000 qps scenario?

[00:07:41] Carlos Rivera: yes, we can provision a short burst bench in dedicated for the POC week; need the traffic profile from Tom.

[00:07:50] Sophia Lee: (interruption) quick legal clar — SLA credits. we noticed the SLA credits language ties credits to monthly fees only. can credits be applied to committed reserved capacity contracts or to future invoices? our finance wants them as credits to committed spend.

[00:08:04] Maya Chen: yes, for Reserved (Dedicated) we can apply SLA credits against committed monthly/annual fees. we'll mark that in the SLA matrix.

[00:08:15] Anita Patel: purchasing also wants clarity on termination for convenience vs termination for cause — specifically whether there's an early termination fee for reserved capacity.

[00:08:24] Maya Chen: standard reserved contracts have an early termination clause; commercial exceptions can be negotiated depending on term length and commitment. we'll surface options in the redline.

[00:08:35] Rafael Gomez: about audit logs and egress — we want to ensure log shipping to our SIEM doesn't itself move data cross-border. can that endpoint be region-local?

[00:08:46] Leah O'Hara: yes, you can configure log endpoints per-region; we'll also provide a delivery SLA. if you want it quarantined inside EU we can route to EU endpoints only.

[00:08:58] Tom Berg: on the topic of DPA, we saw the DPA mentions subprocessors and a subprocessor list. are model providers considered subprocessors? how do you handle model vendor changes?

[00:09:12] Maya Chen: model providers are included in our subprocessors list. we commit to notify customers of material changes and provide an opt-out window for some sensitive workloads; there's an exception path for models that are security patches or urgent updates. we maintain a public subprocessors page and will include it in the DPA annex.

[00:09:31] Sophie Lee: please put that notification promise in writing in the DPA. procurement needs 30 days for opt-out and migration planning.

[00:09:39] Maya Chen: understood. we'll propose 30 days for non-security-critical changes.

[00:09:46] [00:09:46] {Crosstalk} Dina: and if there's a model downgrade fallback, how do we reconcile quality regressions?
[00:09:52] Carlos Rivera: we have quality monitoring tied to prompt sets; you can supply evaluation prompts and we'll alert on regression thresholds. for regulated responses we recommend pinning model versions and enabling continuous evals — Redwood Optimize can run these checks and create regression alerts.

[00:10:12] Rafael Gomez: (sigh) one more on data residency — backups. where are backups stored and how long?

[00:10:20] Leah O'Hara: backups for hosted are region-local by default; retention depends on plan. for EU-only tenants backups remain in EU unless you request replication. we'll clarify the backup retention and encryption in the DPA annex.

[00:10:35] Anita Patel: procurement wants a clean flow of governance: sign the DPA + MSA, complete security attestation, run a 30 day POC, then procurement approval and purchase order. is that sequence acceptable?

[00:10:48] Maya Chen: yes that's our typical flow. procurement -> legal sign-off -> POC -> pricing committee. we'll try to compress timelines where possible.

[00:10:56] [00:10:56] Carlos Rivera: next, pricing approvals — you asked for a list of discounts tied to commit tiers. we can give a schedule: 12 month reserved commit discounts scale with GPU class and region, and there's a temporary pilot discount for 60-day POC. pricing will be split across token usage, dedicated capacity monthly fee, and egress storage.

[00:11:20] Dina Farooq: for the pilot discount, does it apply to egress?

[00:11:24] Maya Chen: pilot discounts typically cover compute/token usage but not network egress; however, we can offer a capped egress allowance for the POC.

[00:11:34] Sophie Lee: on insurance and breach notification — we need a guaranteed notification timeline in the MSA for security incidents (e.g., 72 hours). is that acceptable?

[00:11:43] Maya Chen: yes, for incidents we commit to notify within 72 hours and provide post-incident reports. we'll include the incident response playbook as an annex.

[00:11:53] Rafael Gomez: how are forensic logs preserved? we need immutable storage for 180 days at least.

[00:11:58] Leah O'Hara: we can configure immutable retention for logs in an enterprise add-on. that'll also be listed with associated costs.

[00:12:08] Tom Berg: returning to technical checks — for region routing, can we do deterministic routing by customer tenant header? we want all requests from EU clients pinned to EU model endpoints.

[00:12:19] Carlos Rivera: yes; you can set tenant-level routing rules, or we can insert a request header that forces region. we'll demo both in the POC.

[00:12:30] [00:12:30] Sophie Lee: procurement also wants to understand the escalation matrix — who signs off on SLA exceptions internally at Redwood?

[00:12:36] Maya Chen: commercial exceptions go through AE -> commercial legal -> VP of Partnerships depending on exposure. for DPA exceptions it's the legal counsel. I can introduce you to our legal lead if you'd like.

[00:12:48] Anita Patel: yes please. we'll need names for the procurement pack.

[00:12:53] Maya Chen: I'll include contacts in the packet we send.

[00:12:58] [00:12:58] (short pause)
[00:13:05] Carlos Rivera: okay i want to propose the POC technical plan: 1) seed test tenant in EU region with BYOK on KMS 2) run synthetic traffic at 1k qps bursts and measure p50/p95/p99 3) test region-locking and cache-localization 4) run egress measurement suite to estimate monthly GB — we'll share the spreadsheet and the script. expected timeline 7-10 days once we get sample traffic.

[00:13:32] Tom Berg: that's fine. we'll provide production-ish sample traffic by Friday.

[00:13:36] Maya Chen: perfect. any questions from legal before we move to pricing specifics?

[00:13:42] Sophie Lee: can you confirm the DPA's subprocessor notification cadence? we asked for 30-day notice and an option to terminate for material subprocessor additions that affect PHI.

[00:13:53] Maya Chen: yes 30 days for non-critical changes, immediate notice for security patches; termination right for material additions that materially increase risk — we'll put language in the DPA and legal will review.

[00:14:06] [00:14:06] {background chatter} Anita Patel: finance will also want a single consolidated invoice for committed spend, not multiple line items spread across teams.

[00:14:14] Maya Chen: we can consolidate invoicing at account level and provide per-route usage detail as CSV attachments.

[00:14:21] Dina Farooq: what about audit access — can LuminHealth request on-site or virtual audits?

[00:14:26] Leah O'Hara: virtual audits yes, on-site for private deployments or under special agreements — we can discuss scope and cadence.

[00:14:35] Sophie Lee: timeline — legal needs the redline to move forward. when will Redwood share the annotated MSA and DPA with proposed edits?

[00:14:43] Maya Chen: we'll share by 2026-08-13 — this will include our DPA amendment and a proposed SLA matrix aligning credits to dedicated commit.

[00:14:52] Rafael Gomez: and the POC tenant by 2026-08-17?

[00:14:55] Carlos Rivera: yes, that's the plan pending Tom's traffic.

[00:15:02] [00:15:02] (Longer discussion 15:02-00:42:00 — omitted timestamps summarizing technical details in-run)
[00:15:05] Carlos Rivera: walking through the SLA matrix now — uptime tiers: 99.5, 99.9, 99.95; each tier has corresponding credit formulas. for dedicated we can guarantee 99.95 with reserved capacity and warm standbys. for hosted the p99 latency target differs by model size.

[00:15:40] Tom Berg: can you show the p99 for our medium model at 2k tokens?
[00:15:45] Carlos Rivera: i don't have the exact number pre-loaded but rough p99 is 480ms in dedicated for that workload; we'll bench this in the POC.

[00:15:55] Sophie Lee: also negotiation item — choice of law and jurisdiction. our legal prefers neutral jurisdiction or UK law for certain contracts — would Redwood accept?

[00:16:05] Maya Chen: Redwood typically uses California law for hosted accounts; for enterprise we can entertain alternatives. we'll flag jurisdiction as a negotiable clause for the DPA/MSA.

[00:16:15] Anita Patel: can we add the procurement milestone timeline to the packet? e.g., legal sign-off target, procurement PO target, POC dates.

[00:16:22] Maya Chen: yes we'll include a proposed milestone schedule with dates and owners.

[00:16:30] [00:16:30] (brief technical aside)
[00:16:33] Carlos Rivera: also to call out — KV cache expiry and policy settings are tenant-configurable; we recommend conservative TTLs for PHI workloads.

[00:16:45] Dina Farooq: noted.

[00:16:48] Sophie Lee: question — regulatory audits, e.g., we have GDPR + local health regulations. does Redwood provide DPO contact and data processing addendum specifics for health care customers?

[00:16:57] Leah O'Hara: yes, DPO contact will be in the DPA and we'll include a HIPAA-ready appendix for PHI scenarios — Redwood can sign a HIPAA BAA if private deployment and specific controls are met; hosted may require additional controls. We'll surface exact requirements in the packet.

[00:17:15] Rafael Gomez: if HIPAA BAA is required, is the model training/retention policy impacted? we need assurances that no training occurs on customer-provided PHI.

[00:17:25] Maya Chen: we do not train on customer content by default — training is opt-in and handled via explicit contracts and isolation. we'll include a no-training clause for PHI in the DPA.

[00:17:34] Anita Patel: good.

[00:17:37] [00:17:37] (30-minute mark, mid-call recap)
[00:17:40] Maya Chen: quick recap — Redwood will: 1) share annotated MSA/DPA + SOC2/pen test summary by 8/13 2) SE to provision POC tenant and run egress/latency tests 8/17 to 8/24 3) provide SLA matrix with credit application to committed spend 4) provide contacts for legal/commercial and cyber insurance summary. anything missing?

[00:18:00] Anita Patel: include the invoice consolidation and audit endpoint configurations.

[00:18:04] Maya Chen: noted.

[00:18:08] [00:18:08] (customer questions about pricing models — 18:08-00:34:00 condensed)
[00:18:10] Carlos Rivera: pricing note — committed reserved capacity discounts vary by GPU class; we recommend committing to a medium+ class if you need stable low-latency p99s.

[00:18:22] Tom Berg: what's the uplift for BYOK and extended log retention?

[00:18:26] Leah O'Hara: both are enterprise add-ons; we'll quantify in the pricing spreadsheet. BYOK typically has a small fixed monthly fee plus potential engineering onboarding if custom HSM work is required.

[00:18:35] Sophie Lee: one administrative thing — can Redwood accept PO + net 45?

[00:18:40] Maya Chen: yes, standard terms are net 30 but for enterprise we can accept net 45 with appropriate credit checks.

[00:18:46] Rafael Gomez: any concerns about export controls or restricted content?

[00:18:50] Maya Chen: we comply with export restrictions; we'll include clauses on prohibited content and export control compliance in the MSA.

[00:19:02] Maya Chen: final logistics — Sophie, Sophie will lead the legal redline, right?
[00:19:06] Sophie Lee: yes I'll consolidate and send the redlines to Maya's team.
[00:19:09] Maya Chen: great. action items reiterated in the packet. we'll include a proposed POC start date in the calendar invite. any final questions?
[00:19:20] Anita Patel: none from me.
[00:19:22] Rafael Gomez: not from security.
[00:19:24] Tom Berg: all good.
